Surah Yusuf [Meccan, except verses 1, 2, 3 and 7, which are Medinan; it has 111 verses; it was revealed after Surah Hud]

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra.﴾ Allah knows best what He means by this. ﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾, the Qur'an; the idafa (genitive construction) here carries the sense of "from" (min). ﴿The clear one﴾, the one that makes manifest the truth from falsehood.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 2:

﴿Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an﴾ in the language of the Arabs. ﴿So that you﴾ O people of Mecca ﴿may understand﴾ ﴿taqilun﴾ (you may comprehend) its meanings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 12, verse 3:

﴿Nahnu naqussu ʿalayka aḥsana l-qaṣaṣi bimā awḥaynā﴾ (We relate to you the best of stories through what We have revealed) bi-īḥāʾinā (by Our revelation) ﴿ilayka hādhā l-Qurʾāna wa-in﴾ (to you this Qur'an, and indeed) — mukhaffafa (the particle "in" is here light, i.e., lightened from "inna"), ay wa-innahu (meaning: and indeed it, i.e., and indeed it [the Qur'an] is...)

Remember when Joseph said to his father, Ya'qub, "O my father" (yā abati). The kasra on the "t" indicates the omitted possessive yā' (of the first person, "my"), and the fatha indicates an omitted alif that was converted from a yā'. "Indeed I saw in a dream eleven stars, and the sun and the moon; I saw them" (ra'aytuhum is emphasis), "prostrating to me" (sājidīn). It is pluralized with the yā' and nūn because prostration is an attribute of rational beings.

﴿He said, "My son, do not relate your dream to your brothers, lest they devise a plot against you."﴾ They scheme to destroy you out of envy, because they know its interpretation: that the stars are them, the sun is your mother, and the moon is your father. ﴿Indeed, Satan is a clear enemy to mankind.﴾ Clearly manifest in enmity.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 6:

﴿And thus﴾ as you have seen, ﴿your Lord will choose you﴾ (yakhtaruka) ﴿rabbuka wa-yu'allimuka min ta'wil al-ahadith﴾ the interpretation of dreams (ta'bir al-ru'ya), ﴿and will complete His favour upon you﴾ with prophethood, ﴿and upon the family of Ya'qub﴾ his sons, ﴿as He completed it upon your two fathers﴾ with prophethood, ﴿before, Ibrahim and Ishaq. Indeed your Lord is All-Knowing﴾ of His creation, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in His dealings with them.
﴿Indeed, there was in﴾ the account of ﴿Yusuf and his brothers﴾, and they were eleven, ﴿signs﴾ (lessons) ﴿for those who ask﴾ about their account.

Remember when they said, meaning some of Joseph's brothers said to the others: "Joseph and his brother" — (Joseph is the subject, "mubtada'" (grammatical subject)) — "and his brother" (his full brother, Binyamin) "are dearer" (the predicate, "khabar" (grammatical predicate)) "to our father than we are, though we are a band" (a group), "indeed our father is in clear error" (mistake), "evident," by preferring the two of them over us.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 9:

﴿Kill Joseph or cast him out to some land﴾, meaning, to a distant land, ﴿so that your father's face will be turned toward you﴾, by his coming to you and not turning to anyone else, ﴿and after him you will be a righteous people﴾, meaning, after killing Joseph or casting him out, ﴿by repenting﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 10:

﴿A speaker among them said﴾ He was Yahudha (Judah). ﴿Do not kill Yusuf, but cast him﴾ throw him ﴿into the depths of the well﴾ the dark part of the well. In another recitation (qira'a), it is read in the plural, ﴿ghayabat al-jubb﴾ (the depths of the well), ﴿where some of the travelers will pick him up﴾ the passing travelers, ﴿if you are going to act﴾ to what you intend of separating him from his father. So they were content with that.
﴿They said, "O our father, why do you not trust us with Joseph, when we are indeed sincere toward him?"﴾ [We are indeed] caring for his welfare.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 12:

﴿Send him with us tomorrow﴾ to the desert, ﴿that he may enjoy himself and play﴾ — with the nūn and with the yā' in both verbs — ﴿that he may be active and have fun﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 13:

﴿He said: "Truly, it grieves me that you should take him away"﴾, i.e., your going away ﴿with him﴾, due to separation from him, ﴿and I fear that the wolf may devour him﴾. What is meant by "the wolf" is the species (al-jins), and their land had many wolves, ﴿while you are heedless of him﴾, i.e., preoccupied.

﴿They said: "Surely if the wolf eats him while we are a group (ʿuṣbah)"﴾ — the lām here is a lām of oath (lām qasam) — "a group" meaning a company — ﴿"then indeed we would be losers"﴾, meaning incapable (ʿājizūn). So he sent him with them.

When they had taken him away and agreed to put him into the depths of the well (﴿فَلَمّا ذَهَبُوا بِهِ وأَجْمَعُوا﴾ "when they had taken him away and agreed") — ﴿عَزَمُوا﴾ they resolved — ﴿أنْ يَجْعَلُوهُ فِي غَيابَتِ الجُبّ﴾ "to put him into the depths of the well." The answer to "when" (لَمّا) is omitted, meaning: they did that, by stripping off his shirt after striking and humiliating him and intending to kill him, and they lowered him down. When he reached the middle of the well, they dropped him so that he would die, and he fell into the water, then he took refuge on a rock. They called out to him, and he answered them, thinking they had compassion on him. Then they wanted to crush him with a rock, but Yahudha (Judah) prevented them. ﴿وأَوْحَيْنا إلَيْهِ﴾ "And We revealed to him" — in the well — revelation in its true sense, and he was seventeen years old or less, to reassure his heart — ﴿لَتُنَبَّئَنَّهُمْ﴾ "You will surely inform them" — after this day — ﴿بِأَمْرِهِمْ﴾ "of this their deed" — ﴿هَذا وهُمْ لا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ "while they do not perceive" — that you are the one, at the time of the informing.

"And they came to their father in the evening, weeping." (Qur'an 12:16)

Translation of the commentary:

﴿And they came to their father at ʿishāʾ﴾ (the time of evening)

They said: "O our father, we went racing one another, and left Joseph by our belongings [i.e., our clothes], so the wolf ate him. But you will not believe us, even if we are truthful."

Translation of the commentary:

﴿They said, "O our father, indeed we went off racing [نَسْتَبِق], meaning shooting arrows [نَرْمِي], and we left Joseph by our belongings﴾ [i.e., our clothes] ﴿and the wolf ate him. And you will not believe [بِمُؤْمِنٍ, i.e., give credence to] us﴾ ﴿even if we were truthful﴾ [i.e., in your view]; you would have accused us regarding this story because of your love for Joseph. So how (would you believe us), when you think badly of us?"

﴿And they came upon his shirt﴾. Its position is in the accusative (naṣb) as an adverb of place (ẓarfiyyah), meaning "upon it" (fawqahu), ﴿with false blood﴾, meaning blood that is false (dhī kadhib). They had slaughtered a young goat (sakhlah), smeared his shirt with its blood, forgot to tear the shirt, and claimed, "It is his blood." ﴿He said﴾, meaning Ya'qub, when he saw the shirt intact and knew their lie: ﴿Rather, your souls have embellished for you a matter﴾, meaning made it seem appealing to you, ﴿so you did it to him.﴾ ﴿So patience is beautiful﴾, meaning without any lamenting. It is the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada'), meaning "my matter is patience that is beautiful." ﴿And God is the One whose help is sought﴾, meaning the One from whom aid is required ﴿against what you describe﴾, meaning what you mention of the matter of Yusuf.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 19:

﴿And there came a caravan﴾ travelers from Madyan (Midian) toward Egypt, and they camped near the well of Yusuf. ﴿So they sent their water-drawer﴾ the one who comes to the water to draw from it. ﴿And he let down his bucket﴾ he sent his bucket into the well, and Yusuf clung to it, so he drew him up. ﴿When he saw him, he said: "O joy!"﴾ and in another reading it is "Bushra" (good news); the calling out to it is figurative, meaning: "Come forth, for this is your time." ﴿This is a boy!﴾ So his brothers came to know of him and came to him. ﴿And they concealed him﴾ meaning they hid his matter, making him ﴿a commodity﴾ by saying, "This is our slave who ran away." Yusuf remained silent out of fear that they would kill him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, the "Commentary of the Two Jalals") on Surah 12 (Yusuf), verse 20:

﴿And they sold him﴾ to them ﴿for a deficient price﴾, ﴿a few counted dirhams﴾, twenty or twenty-two. ﴿And they were among those who had no desire for him﴾, that is, his brothers. The caravan brought him to Egypt, and the one who bought him sold him for twenty dinars, two pairs of sandals and two garments.

And the one who bought him from Egypt, who was Qitfir, the Aziz (the minister), said to his wife, Zulaykha, "Make his stay honorable; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son," and he was ḥaṣūr (one incapable of intercourse). ﴿And thus﴾, just as We rescued him from being killed and from the well, and inclined the heart of the Aziz toward him, ﴿We established Joseph in the land﴾, the land of Egypt, until he attained what he attained. ﴿And that We may teach him the interpretation (ta'wīl) of events﴾, meaning the interpretation of dreams. This is conjoined (ʿuṭifa) to an implied element connected with "We established," meaning "so that We may make him king," or the waw is extra. ﴿And Allah is dominant over His affair﴾, exalted above all, nothing can overpower Him. ﴿But most of mankind﴾, who are the disbelievers, ﴿do not know﴾ this.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 22:

﴿And when he reached his maturity﴾, and that is thirty years or thirty-three, ﴿We gave him judgment﴾, meaning wisdom, ﴿and knowledge﴾, meaning understanding of the religion, before he was sent as a prophet. ﴿And thus﴾, as We rewarded him, ﴿We reward the good-doers﴾, those who do good for their own souls.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 23:

﴿And she, in whose house he was, sought to seduce him﴾ — she was Zulaykha — ﴿from himself﴾, meaning she asked him to lie with her, ﴿and she closed the doors﴾ of the house, ﴿and said﴾ to him, ﴿"Come, you!"﴾ meaning hasten (halumm), and the lam (in laka) is for explanation (al-tabyin). It is also read with a kasra on the ha' (hay'a) and in another reading with a damma on the ta' (hayta). ﴿He said: "God forbid!"﴾ meaning I seek refuge in God from that. ﴿Indeed, he﴾ — the one who bought me — ﴿my lord﴾, my master, ﴿has made my abode good﴾, my dwelling, so I will not betray him regarding his household. ﴿Indeed, the matter﴾ — that is, the situation — ﴿the wrongdoers will not prosper﴾, meaning the fornicators.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 24:

﴿And indeed, she desired him,﴾ meaning she intended intercourse with him. ﴿And he would have desired her﴾ meaning he intended that too, ﴿had he not seen the proof of his Lord.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: Yaʿqub was made visible to him, so he struck his chest, and his desire came out from his fingertips. The answer to ﴿lawla﴾ (had it not been) is: he would have lain with her. ﴿Thus﴾ We showed him the proof, ﴿that We might turn away from him evil﴾ betrayal, ﴿and immorality﴾ fornication. ﴿Indeed, he was among Our devoted servants﴾ in obedience. And in another reading, with a fatha on the lam, meaning: those who were chosen.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (the exegesis of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 12, verse 25:

﴿And they raced to the door﴾: Yusuf hastened toward it to flee, and she hastened after him to seize hold of him. So she caught hold of his garment and pulled him toward her. ﴿And she tore his shirt from behind﴾: she split it. ﴿And they met her husband at the door﴾: they found her master, her husband, there. So she declared herself innocent, then ﴿said, "What is the penalty for one who intended evil for your wife?"﴾: meaning adultery. ﴿Except that he be imprisoned﴾: confined in a prison, ﴿or a painful punishment﴾: painful, by being beaten.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 26:

﴿He said﴾ Yusuf, clearing himself, ﴿"It was she who sought to seduce me from myself." And a witness from her own family testified﴾, the son of her paternal uncle. It is related that he was in the cradle, and he said, ﴿"If his shirt is torn from the front"﴾, i.e., from in front,
﴿And if his shirt is torn from behind﴾ from the back.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 28:

﴿When he saw his shirt torn from behind﴾ — [i.e., when the husband] ﴿he said: "Indeed, it is﴾ — i.e., your saying — ﴿the recompense of one who intended﴾ — etc. — ﴿evil for your wife, except that he be imprisoned or [suffer] a painful punishment?"﴾ — ﴿of your guile, O women.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 29:

﴿Yūsuf, turn away from this﴾ matter, and do not mention it, lest it spread. ﴿And ask forgiveness﴾ O Zulaykha ﴿for your sin. Indeed, you were of the sinners﴾, the guilty ones. And the news became famous and spread.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 30:

﴿And women said in the city﴾ the city of Egypt. ﴿The wife of the chief minister is seeking to seduce her young man﴾ her slave. ﴿From himself. He has inflamed her with love﴾ a specification (tamyiz); that is, his love has penetrated the shaghaf of her heart, i.e. its covering. ﴿Indeed, we see her in manifest error﴾ i.e. in error, ﴿clear﴾ evident, by her love for him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 31:

﴿When she heard of their scheming﴾, their backbiting about her, ﴿she sent for them and prepared﴾ prepared ﴿for them a reclining-cushion﴾, food cut with a knife for reclining upon it, and it was the citron (utrujj); ﴿and gave each one of them a knife﴾ gave ﴿each one of them a knife, and said﴾ to Yusuf, ﴿Come out before them.﴾ ﴿So when they saw him, they were amazed at him﴾ magnified him, ﴿and cut their hands﴾ with the knives, and they did not feel the pain because their hearts were occupied with Yusuf. ﴿And they said: Hashā lillāh!﴾ meaning, glory be to Allah, exalting Him, ﴿This is not a human being; this is none other than a noble angel.﴾ because of the beauty he possessed, which does not normally exist in a human being. And in a hadith: (He was given half of beauty).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 32:

﴿She said﴾ the wife of the Chief (al-'Aziz), when she saw what had befallen them, ﴿"That is he, the one about whom you blamed me"﴾, i.e. this is he about whose love you reproached me; this is an explanation of her excuse. ﴿"And I did seek to seduce him, but he refused"﴾ he abstained (istaʿṣama). ﴿"And if he does not do what I command him"﴾ to do, ﴿"he will certainly be imprisoned and will certainly be among the debased"﴾, the humiliated. ﴿So they said, "Obey your mistress."﴾

﴿He said, "My Lord, the prison is dearer to me than that to which they invite me. And unless You turn their plotting away from me, I would incline toward them and be among the ignorant."﴾ أمِلْ (Incline) ﴿toward them﴾ ﴿and I would be﴾ أصِرْ (become) ﴿among the ignorant﴾ المُذْنِبِينَ (the sinners). The purpose of this statement is supplication, and therefore the Exalted said:
﴿So his Lord responded to him﴾ [to] his supplication. ﴿So He turned away from him their plot. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾ of the speech, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of the deed.

Then it appeared to them, after they had seen the signs (the evidences indicating Yusuf's innocence), that they should imprison him. This indicated the statement: ﴿Surely they shall imprison him for a time﴾, until ﴿a time﴾ at which people's talk about him would cease. So he was imprisoned.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 36:

﴿And there entered with him into the prison two young men.﴾ Two servants of the king (al-malik), one of whom was his cupbearer (sāqīhi) and the other his food-steward (ṣāḥib ṭaʿāmihi). They saw him interpreting dreams, so they said, "Let us test him." ﴿One of them said﴾, and he was the cupbearer, ﴿"Indeed I see myself pressing wine."﴾ That is, grapes. ﴿And the other said﴾, and he was the food-steward, ﴿"Indeed I see myself carrying bread upon my head, of which the birds eat. Inform us﴾ tell us ﴿of its interpretation﴾ of its ta'wīl (interpretation), i.e., its ta'bīr (dream-interpretation)."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 37:

﴿He said﴾ to the two of them, informing them that he knows the interpretation of dreams: ﴿No food will come to you that you are provided with﴾ in your sleep ﴿except that I will inform you of its interpretation﴾ while awake ﴿before it comes to you﴾ its interpretation. ﴿That is of what my Lord has taught me.﴾ In this is an exhortation to their belief; then he strengthened it with his saying ﴿Indeed, I have abandoned the religion﴾ (dīn) ﴿of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they, in the Hereafter, they﴾ (is) an emphasis.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 38:

﴿And I have followed the religion of my forefathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. It is not for us to associate anything with Allah﴾ yanbaghi (it is befitting) ﴿for us to associate⦗with Allah⦘ from﴾ min, which is extra (za'ida) ﴿anything﴾ shay'. ﴿That⦗, the monotheism⦘⦗ is⦘ from the bounty of Allah upon us and upon mankind, but most of mankind⦗, who are the disbelievers,⦘ ﴿do not give thanks﴾ to Allah, so they associate⦗ partners with Him⦘. Then he explicitly called them to belief in the following words:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 39:

﴿O my two fellow prisoners!﴾ (i.e., my two companions who dwell in) ﴿the prison: Are lords who are diverse better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ "Better" is an interrogative of affirmation (istifham taqrir).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 40:

﴿What you worship besides Him﴾, i.e., other than Him, ﴿are only names you have named﴾, you have named by them idols, ﴿you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾, for worshipping them, ﴿no proof or evidence﴾. ﴿Judgment﴾, i.e., the decision, ﴿is for none but Allah alone. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. That﴾, i.e., this monotheism, ﴿is the correct religion﴾, the upright one, ﴿but most of mankind﴾, who are the disbelievers, ﴿do not know﴾ what punishment they are heading toward, so they associate partners with Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 41:

﴿O my two fellow prisoners! As for one of you, he will go out after three days and will give his lord (sayyid) wine to drink as is his habit.﴾ ﴿And as for the other, he will go out after three days and be crucified, and birds will eat from his head.﴾ This is the interpretation of your two dreams. They said, "We saw nothing." He said, ﴿The matter has been decided (qudiya), (meaning) completed, about which you two inquire﴾, whether you spoke the truth or lied.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 42:

﴿And he said to the one he thought would be saved from the two﴾ [i.e., was certain (ayqana)] ﴿that he was saved from them﴾ [and he was the cupbearer (al-saqi)] ﴿"Mention me to your lord"﴾ [i.e., your master], so tell him: "Indeed there is in the prison a youth who has been imprisoned unjustly." So he went out. ﴿But Satan caused him to forget the mention﴾ [i.e., the cupbearer's] ﴿of his lord﴾ [i.e., mentioning Yusuf to his lord]. ﴿So he remained﴾ [he stayed; Yusuf remained] ﴿in the prison for several years﴾ [it was said: seven years, and it was said: twelve].

﴿And the king said﴾, the king of Egypt, al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid, ﴿"Indeed, I see﴾, i.e., I saw, ﴿seven fat cows which are being eaten by seven lean ones﴾, i.e., swallowing them, ﴿seven﴾ of the cows ﴿lean﴾, the plural of ʿajfāʾ, ﴿and seven green spikes and others dry﴾, i.e., seven spikes that are ﴿dry﴾, having twisted around the green ones and overcome them. ﴿"O eminent ones, explain to me my vision﴾, make clear to me its interpretation, ﴿if you are able to interpret visions"﴾, so interpret them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 44:

﴿They said﴾ these are ﴿confused dreams﴾ mixtures (akhlat).

ـ﴿And the one of the two who had been saved said﴾: that is, of the two youths, and he was the cupbearer. ﴿and remembered﴾ after a period of time: in it there is substitution, the taa' originally being a daal, and its assimilation into the daal; that is, he remembered (tadhakkara) ﴿after a while﴾, when Yusuf's situation came to mind. ﴿"I will inform you of its interpretation, so send me forth"﴾, so they sent him, and he came to Yusuf and said:

O Joseph, you truthful one (al-Siddiq), the one who is very truthful, give us your interpretation concerning seven fat cows which are eaten by seven green ears of grain and others dry, so that I may return to the people (i.e., the king and his companions) so that they may know its interpretation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 47:

﴿He said: "You will sow for seven years in succession"﴾, meaning: sow. ﴿Continuously﴾ means consecutively, and this is the interpretation of the seven fat cows. ﴿Then whatever you harvest, leave it in its ears﴾, meaning: leave it. ﴿Except a little of what you eat﴾, so thresh it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 48:

﴿Then there will come after that﴾, i.e., after the seven fertile years, ﴿seven hard [years]﴾, barren and difficult, and these are the interpretation of the seven lean [cows]. ﴿They will consume what you have stored up for them﴾ of the grain sown during the fertile years, i.e., you will eat it during them, ﴿except a little of what you preserve﴾, i.e., what you save up (tadakhkhirun, "store").

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 49:

﴿Then after that there will come a year in which the people will be given rain, and in which they will press (juice).﴾ That is, after the seven barren years. "In which the people will be given rain" means with rain. "And in which they will press" means they will press grapes and other produce, because of its abundance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 50:

﴿And the king said﴾ when the messenger came to him and informed him of its interpretation, ﴿"Bring him to me"﴾, i.e., the one who interpreted it. ﴿So when the messenger came to him﴾, i.e., Yusuf, ﴿the messenger﴾ and requested that he come out, ﴿he said﴾, intending to make his innocence manifest, ﴿"Return to your lord and ask him"﴾ to inquire ﴿"what is the case of the women who cut their hands? Indeed my Lord"﴾ my master ﴿"is Knowing of their plot."﴾ So he returned and informed the king, and he gathered them.

﴿He said, "What was your affair when you sought to seduce Yusuf from himself? Did you find in him any inclination toward you?"﴾ *Sha'nukunna*: your matter.

﴿They said, "Allah forbid! We know no evil in him."﴾ The wife of al-'Aziz said, ﴿"Now the truth has become manifest"﴾, meaning it became clear, ﴿"It was I who sought to seduce him from himself, and he is surely among the truthful"﴾ regarding his saying, ﴿"It was she who sought to seduce me from myself"﴾. So Yusuf was informed of that, and said

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 52:

﴿That﴾ i.e., the request for exoneration, ﴿so that he [al-ʿAzīz] may know that I did not betray him﴾ regarding his household ﴿in his absence﴾ (bi-l-ghayb), which is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). Then he humbled himself before God and said:

Qur'anic quotations, with their meanings:

﴿And I do not declare myself innocent﴾ of error. ﴿Indeed, the soul﴾ (the genus of souls) ﴿is certainly one that commands evil﴾ a great deal ﴿except for those on whom my Lord has mercy﴾, so that He protects them.

Note on the translation: "إلّا ما" here is read with "ما" in the sense of "مَن" (those whom), as the commentary indicates, and "الجِنْس" is glossed as the genus of souls, meaning the soul as a category rather than one particular soul.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 54:

﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me; I will take him exclusively for myself."﴾ I will make him sincerely mine, with no partner. So the messenger came to him and said, "Answer the king." He stood up, bade farewell to the people of the prison, and prayed for them. Then he bathed, put on fine clothes, and entered upon the king. ﴿So when he spoke with him, he said﴾ to him, ﴿"Indeed, you are today with us established and trusted."﴾ Possessing standing and trustworthiness, [entrusted] with our affairs. "So what do you see we should do?" He said, "Gather the food and sow a great amount of crops in these fertile years, and store the grain in its ears, so that people will come to you to obtain provisions from you." He said, "Who will be responsible for this for me?"

Yusuf said: "Set me over the treasuries of the land" — the land of Egypt — "Indeed I am a guardian, knowing" — possessing protection and knowledge of its affairs. It was also said: a scribe, a reckoner.

Thus did We establish Joseph in the land, [meaning, just as We favoured him by delivering him from prison] ﴿Thus﴾ [like Our bestowal upon him of deliverance from the prison] ﴿We established Joseph in the land﴾ [the land of Egypt], ﴿to settle therein wherever he willed﴾ [to dwell in it], after hardship and imprisonment. In the narrative: the king [of Egypt] came to him, sealed his hand [in token of authority], appointed him in place of the Aziz (al-'Aziz, the governor) and dismissed the latter; then the Aziz died, and [the king] married him to his wife, and he found her a virgin, and she bore him two sons. He upheld justice in Egypt, and necks bowed down to him.
﴿And the reward of the Hereafter is better﴾ than the reward of this world. The years of famine had set in, and it struck the land of Canaan and al-Sham (Syria).

And the brothers of Joseph came, except Binyamin, to buy provisions (al-mirah, grain for provisions), since news had reached them that the governor of Egypt was giving out food in exchange for payment. ﴿So they entered upon him, and he recognised them,﴾ that they were his brothers, ﴿while they did not recognise him,﴾ for they did not know him, because a long time had passed since they had last seen him and they thought he had perished. They spoke to him in Hebrew (al-'Ibraniyya). He said, as one who disclaims them: "What has brought you to my land?" They said: "For provisions." He said: "Perhaps you are spies ('uyun)." They said: "God forbid!" He said: "Then where are you from?" They said: "From the land of Kan'an, and our father is Ya'qub, a prophet of God." He said: "And does he have other sons besides you?" They said: "Yes. We were twelve. Our youngest went off and was lost in the desert, and he was the most beloved of us to him. His full brother remained, and he kept him back so that he might be comforted by him in place of the other." So he ordered that they be lodged and honoured.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 12, verse 59:

﴿And when he had furnished them with their provisions,﴾ he gave them full measure of their grain. ﴿He said: "Bring me a brother of yours from your father.﴾ That is, Binyamin (Benjamin), ﴿so that I may know the truth of what you have said.﴾ ﴿Do you not see that I give full measure, and that I am the best of hosts?﴾ I complete the measure without any shortfall.

﴿But if you do not bring him to me, then there will be no measure [of grain] for you from me, and do not come near me.﴾ I.e., provision (ميرة).

"Do not come near me" is either a prohibition (نَهْي), or it is conjoined (عَطْف) to the grammatical position (مَحَلّ) of "then there will be no measure for you," meaning: you will be deprived, and you will not come near.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 61:

﴿They said: "We will seek to persuade our father to let him go; and indeed, we will do it."﴾ "We will exert ourselves in seeking him from him," and "indeed, we will do that."

And he said to his servants, (in another reading, "to his attendants," meaning his boys) "Put their merchandise [i.e., the money they brought as the price of the grain], which was in dirhams, into their saddlebags (rihal, i.e., their baggage), so that they may recognize it when they return to their families, and unpack their baggage, so that they may come back to us," because they would not consider it lawful to keep it.

When they returned to their father, they said, "O our father, the measure has been withheld from us (i.e., if you do not send our brother with us to him), so send our brother with us and we will get our measure," with the nūn and the yā' (i.e., "nakhtal" and "yaktal," both readings of the verb for measuring out).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 64:

﴿He said: "Shall I trust you with him any more than I trusted you with his brother before?"﴾ ﴿Is it so?﴾ Meaning: "Shall I entrust him to you, when I did not entrust him to you before?" [He said]: "Shall I entrust him to you," ﴿as I entrusted you with his brother Yusuf before?﴾ ﴿before﴾ although you had done to him what you did. ﴿But Allah is the best guardian﴾ and in another reading, ﹙ḥifẓan﹚ is a specification (tamyiz), like their saying "Lillahi darruh fārisan" (How excellent he is as a horseman). ﴿And He is the most merciful of the merciful﴾ so I hope that He will bestow upon me His protection of him.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 12, verse 65:

﴿When they opened their goods, they found their merchandise had been returned to them. They said, "O our father, what more could we want? This is our merchandise, returned to us. We will bring provisions for our family, guard our brother, and gain an extra camel-load. That is an easy measure."﴾

"Ma" here is interrogative (istifhamiyyah), meaning: what thing could we seek beyond the honour of the king? Nothing is greater than this. It is also read with a ta' (tu-) as direct address to Ya'qub, since they had mentioned to him the honour shown to them.

﴿This is our merchandise, returned to us. We will bring provisions for our family⁠—⁠(namir ahlana) we will bring the mirah (provisions) for them, which is food.﴾ ﴿And guard our brother and gain an extra camel-load⁠—⁠(li-akhina) for our brother.﴾ ﴿That is an easy measure⁠—⁠(sahl) easy for the king, owing to his generosity.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 66:

﴿He said: "I will never send him with you until you give me a solemn pledge in God's name, that you will surely bring him back to me, unless you are encircled [by some calamity]."﴾ A covenant (ʿahdan) ﴿in God's name﴾, by swearing ﴿that you will surely bring him back to me, unless you are encircled﴾ [by death], i.e., you die or are overpowered so that you are unable to bring him. ﴿So when they had given him their pledge﴾ to that effect, ﴿he said: "God is Witness over what we say"﴾ between us and you, ﴿a Guardian (wakil)﴾, a Witness; and he sent him with them.

﴿And he said, "O my sons, do not enter﴾ [Egypt] ﴿through one gate, but enter through separate gates﴾, so that the evil eye (al-'ayn) does not afflict you. ﴿And I cannot avail you anything against Allah﴾, i.e., I cannot repel from you ﴿by this statement of mine any [thing]﴾, where ﴿min﴾ is a redundant particle (za'ida), ﴿decreed for you by Allah﴾. This advice was only out of compassion. ﴿In﴾ (i.e., "not," equivalent to "ma") ﴿judgment belongs only to Allah﴾ alone. ﴿In Him I have put my trust﴾, relying on Him and placing my confidence in Him.

﴿When they entered from where their father had commanded them﴾, i.e., separately. ﴿It would not have availed them anything against Allah﴾, i.e., against His decree. ﴿مِن﴾ is ziyadah (superfluous). ﴿Anything, except﴾ (but) ﴿a need in the soul of Ya'qub, which he fulfilled﴾, and it was the desire to ward off the evil eye, out of compassion. ﴿And indeed he was a possessor of knowledge through what We had taught him﴾, because of Our teaching him. ﴿But most people﴾, who are the disbelievers, ﴿do not know﴾ the ilham (divine inspiration) of Allah to His asfiya' (chosen ones).

When they entered upon Yusuf, he drew his brother close to him (﴿آوى﴾ means he took him in, ﴿ضَمَّ﴾) and said: ﴿Indeed, I am your brother, so do not grieve﴾ (﴿تَبْتَئِس﴾ means grieve) ﴿over what they used to do﴾ ﴿مِن الحَسَد لَنا﴾, that is, out of envy toward us. He commanded him not to inform them, and they agreed together that he would devise a plan to keep him with himself.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 70:

﴿So when he had furnished them with their provisions, he placed the drinking-cup﴾ it was a gold measuring-vessel set with jewels ﴿in the saddlebag of his brother﴾ Binyamin ﴿Then a caller called out﴾ a crier called out after they had departed from the assembly of Yusuf ﴿O caravan﴾ the company of travellers
﴿They said, and﴾ [they had] ﴿come up to them﴾, "What is it that you are missing?" The pronoun ـه ("it") is attached to ﴿تفقدون﴾, so the full sense is ﴿تفقدونه﴾, "you are missing it."
They said, "We have missed the king's measuring cup (ṣuwāʿ), and for whoever brings it is a camel-load [of food], and I am its guarantor (zaʿīm)," that is, its surety (kafīl) for the load.

﴿They said, "By God!"﴾ an oath containing the sense of wonder (ta'ajjub). ﴿You certainly know that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, and that we were not thieves﴾, we had never stolen at all.

﴿They said﴾, i.e., the caller (al-Mu'adhdhin) and his companions, ﴿"What is the recompense for him?"﴾, i.e., for the thief, ﴿"if you are liars?"﴾ in your saying, "We were not thieves," and [the cup] was found among you.

They said, "Its recompense is: he in whose saddlebag it is found, he himself is its recompense." ﴿They said, "Its recompense is..."﴾ Here *jaza'uhu* (its recompense) is the *mubtada'* (subject of the nominal sentence), and *man wujida fi rahlihi* (he in whose baggage it is found) is its *khabar* (predicate). The clause is then emphasized by His words ﴿fa-huwa jaza'uhu﴾ (he himself is its recompense), where *fa-huwa* refers to the thief, meaning that the recompense is the stolen item and nothing else. The custom of the family of Ya'qub was ﴿Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾, referring to recompense for theft. They then openly asked Yusuf to search their bags.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 76:

﴿So he began with their bags﴾ and searched them, ﴿before his brother's bag﴾ so that he would not be accused, ﴿then he brought it out﴾, i.e. the drinking-cup (al-siqaya). ﴿Thus did We devise﴾ the scheme ﴿for Joseph﴾, We taught him the stratagem (al-ihtiyal) for taking his brother, ﴿for he could not have taken his brother﴾ Joseph could not have, ﴿under the king's law﴾, i.e. the ruling of the king of Egypt, gently (raqiqan) from theft, ﴿because the penalty for it in his judgement was beating and fining double the value of the stolen goods, not enslavement﴾, ﴿except that God willed it﴾, i.e. taking him by the ruling of his father. That is, he could not take him except by the will of God, by His inspiration, [after] the questioning of his brothers and their answer according to their own custom. ﴿We raise in degrees whom We will﴾, with the idafa and with tanwin in knowledge, as with Joseph, ﴿and above every possessor of knowledge﴾ among created beings ﴿is one who knows﴾ more than him, until it ends with God Most High.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 77:

﴿They said: "If he steals, a brother of his has stolen before"﴾ i.e., Yusuf. He had stolen for his mother's father an idol of gold and broke it, lest he worship it.

﴿So Yusuf kept it within himself and did not reveal it﴾ i.e., did not make it apparent ﴿to them﴾. The pronoun refers to the statement in His words "They said." ﴿He said﴾ within himself: ﴿"You are worse in position"﴾ than Yusuf and his brother, due to your stealing your brother from your father and your wronging him. ﴿And Allah is most knowing﴾ and aware ﴿of what you describe﴾, i.e., what you mention of his matter.

They said, "O Chief of Egypt, indeed he has an aged father, a great old man, who loves him more than us, and he is consoled by him for his lost son, and his separation from him grieves him. So take one of us in his place," enslave him instead of him, "for indeed we see you are among the good-doers," in your actions.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 79:

﴿He said: "We seek refuge in Allah"﴾ It is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), its verb deleted and it being annexed to the object; i.e., "We seek refuge in Allah from ﴿that we should take anyone except him with whom we found our property﴾." He did not say "whoever stole," to avoid lying. ﴿Indeed, we would then be wrongdoers﴾ if we took other than him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 80:

﴿When they despaired of him⟩ they gave up hope, ﴿they withdrew⟩ they separated themselves from others, ﴿to consult privately⟩ a verbal noun (maṣdar) that may be used for the singular and other than it, meaning that some of them were conferring with one another in private. ﴿Their eldest said⟩ in age, Rubeel, or in opinion: Yahudha (Judah). ﴿Do you not know that your father has taken from you a solemn pledge⟩ a covenant ﴿before God⟩ concerning your brother, ﴿and before this⟩ the word "mā" is superfluous (zāʾida), though it has also been said that "mā" is a verbal particle (maṣdariyya) serving as the subject, with "min qabl" as its predicate, ﴿so I will not leave⟩ I will not depart from ﴿the land⟩ the land of Egypt ﴿until my father gives me leave⟩ to return to him, ﴿or God judges for me⟩ regarding the deliverance of my brother, ﴿and He is the best of judges⟩ the most just of them.

Return to your father and say: "O our father, your son has stolen, and we testify only to what we know. And we were not guardians over the unseen." [We testify only to what we know] with certainty, from seeing the cup in his baggage. [And we were not guardians over the unseen] of what was hidden from us at the time the covenant was given. [Had we known he would steal, we would not have taken him.]

﴿And ask the town in which we were﴾: it is Egypt. That is, send [someone] to its people and ask them. ﴿And the caravan﴾: the people of the caravan ﴿in which we travelled﴾, and they were a people from Canaan. ﴿And indeed we are truthful﴾ in what we say. So they returned to him and told him that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 83:

﴿He said, "Rather, your souls have beautified⁠ for you⁠ a matter"﴾ (zayyanat lakum anfusukum amran), meaning: made it seem good to you, so you did it. He accused them because of what had preceded from them regarding the matter of Yusuf. ﴿So patience is beautiful﴾ (sabrun jamil), meaning: my patience is beautiful. ﴿Perhaps Allah will bring them to me all together﴾ (bi-Yusuf wa-akhawayhi jami'an), meaning: Yusuf and his two brothers. ﴿Indeed He is the All-Knowing﴾ (al-'Alim), of my condition, ﴿the All-Wise﴾ (al-Hakim), in His creation.

And he turned away from them, abandoning addressing them, and said, "Oh, my grief (ya asafa)" — the alif is substituted for the ya' of possession, meaning "O my grief" — "over Joseph." And his eyes turned white, meaning their blackness was obliterated and replaced by whiteness from his weeping, "from the grief over him." "So he was suppressing it" — (kazim): distressed, afflicted, not showing his anguish.

﴿They said, "By God, you will not cease﴾ [لا تَفْتَأ, meaning "continue"] ﴿remembering Joseph until you become﴾ [حَرَضًا, meaning] ﴿a wasted one﴾ [مُشْرِفًا عَلى الهَلاك, meaning "near to destruction"] because of the length of your illness. [حَرَضًا] is a verbal noun (مَصْدَر, a noun derived from a verb), in which the singular and the plural are alike. ﴿Or you become one of the dead﴾ [الهالِكِينَ, meaning] the ones who have died.

He said, "I only complain of my anguish and my grief to Allah, [i.e., it is] the great sorrow that he cannot bear to keep hidden and so it is spread among people, [and] my grief is to Allah, not to anyone else, for it is He to whom complaint benefits. And I know from Allah what you do not know," namely that the dream of Yusuf is true and that he is alive. Then he said:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 87:

﴿O my sons, go and search for news of Joseph and his brother﴾ seek out their news; ﴿and do not despair of relief from Allah﴾ do not give up hope; ﴿from Allah's mercy﴾ His compassion. So they set off towards Egypt, to (look for) Joseph.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 88:

﴿So when they entered upon him, they said: "O 'Aziz (ruler), hardship has touched us and our family, and we have come with poor merchandise (goods), so give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable."﴾ "Hardship" means hunger. "Poor merchandise" means merchandise that is rejected, which everyone who sees it pushes away because of its poor quality; it was dirhams that were counterfeit or other than that. "Give us full measure" means complete for us the measure, "and be charitable to us" by overlooking the poor quality of our merchandise. "Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable" means He gives them reward. So he (Yusuf) was moved with compassion for them, mercy overtook him, and he lifted the veil between him and them.

Then he said to them, rebuking them: "Do you know what you did to Joseph" by way of beating and selling him and other than that, "and to his brother" by way of your wronging him after the separation from his brother, "when you were ignorant?" of what the outcome of Joseph's affair would be.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 90:

﴿They said﴾ after they had recognised him from what appeared of his features, seeking certainty. ﴿Are you indeed⁠—﴾ with both hamzahs pronounced fully (تحقيق الهمزتين, *tahqiq al-hamzatayn*), or with the second softened (تسهيل الثانية, *tashil al-thaniya*), and with an alif inserted between them, in both readings: ﴿are you indeed Yusuf?⁠﴾ He said: I am Yusuf, and this is my brother. God has indeed bestowed favour upon us by bringing us together. ﴿Indeed, whoever fears God and is patient⁠—﴾ God does not waste the reward of the good-doers. In it is the placing of the apparent noun in the place of the pronoun (وضع الظاهر موضع المضمر, *wad' al-zahir mawdi' al-mudmar*).

They said: "By God, God has certainly preferred you over us" [﴿آثَرَك﴾ means: favoured you (فَضَّلَك) ﴿اللَّه عَلَيْنا﴾ with kingship and other things], "and indeed" [﴿وإنْ﴾ is lightened (مُخَفَّفَة), meaning: indeed (أيْ إنّا)] "we were certainly sinners" [﴿كُنّا لَخاطِئِينَ﴾ meaning: guilty (آثِمِينَ) in your matter, so we humiliated you].

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 12, verse 92:

﴿He said, "There is no reproach (*tathrib*, meaning *'atab*, blame) against you today."﴾ He singled out "today" for mention because it is the occasion for reproach, so the reproach for other times is all the more unlikely. He asked them about his father, and they said, "His eyes have gone white," so he said:

﴿Go with this shirt of mine﴾. It is the shirt of Ibrahim, which he wore when he was thrown into the fire. It was on his neck in the well, and it is from Paradise. Jibril commanded that it be sent, and said: "Indeed, in it is its scent, and it is not placed upon one afflicted except that he is cured." ﴿Then cast it over my father's face; he will come back seeing﴾.

And when the caravan departed [from the outskirts of Egypt], their father said [to those of his sons and grandsons present]: ﴿Indeed, I find the scent of Joseph﴾ — the breeze carried it to him from a distance of three days, or eight, or more, by God's leave — ﴿were it not that you think me senile﴾ — that you deem me foolish — you would believe me.

﴿They said﴾ to him, ﴿"By God, you are in your old error"﴾ — that is, in your old mistake, ﴿"the ancient"﴾ — arising from your excessive love for him and your hope of meeting him despite the long passage of time.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 12, verse 96:

﴿Then when﴾ *[the particle]* ﴿an﴾ is superfluous (*zā'idah*, a particle that adds no meaning) ﴿the bearer of good news came﴾, Yahudha, ﴿with the shirt﴾. He had been carrying the shirt stained with blood, so he wished to gladden him as he had grieved him. ﴿He cast it﴾, meaning he threw the shirt, ﴿over his face, and he returned﴾, meaning his sight returned.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 98:

﴿He said: "I shall ask my Lord to forgive you. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ He postponed that until the last part of the night (al-sahar), so that it would be closer to being answered, or until the night of Friday. Then they set out toward Egypt (Misr), and Yusuf and the dignitaries went out to meet them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 12, verse 99:

﴿When they entered upon Yusuf﴾ in his tent, ﴿he drew his two parents close to him﴾, his father and his mother, or his maternal aunt. ﴿And he said﴾ to them, ﴿"Enter Egypt, if God wills, in security"﴾. So they entered, and Yusuf sat upon his throne.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 100:

﴿And he raised his parents high upon the throne﴾ he seated them with him ﴿upon the throne﴾, the couch. ﴿And they fell down before him in prostration﴾, i.e., his parents and his brothers. ﴿Prostration﴾ of bowing, not placing the forehead on the ground; and that was their greeting in that time. ﴿And he said: "O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision from before; my Lord has made it true, and He has been good to me﴾ to me ﴿when He brought me out of the prison﴾; he did not say "out of the well," out of generosity, lest his brothers be embarrassed. ﴿And He brought you from the desert﴾, the desert country ﴿after Satan had sown discord﴾, caused corruption ﴿between me and my brothers. Indeed my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed He is the All-Knowing﴾ of His creation ﴿the All-Wise﴾ in His making." And his father remained with him twenty-four years, or seventeen years, and the period of their separation was eighteen years, or forty years, or eighty years. When death approached him, he charged Yusuf to carry him and bury him beside his father, so he went himself and buried him there. Then he returned to Egypt and remained after him twenty-three years. When his affair was complete and he knew that it would not last, his soul yearned for the everlasting kingdom, so he said:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 101:

﴿My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom and taught me of the interpretation of events﴾, meaning the interpretation of dreams. ﴿Originator (Fatir) of the heavens and the earth, You are my Guardian (Wali)﴾, meaning the one who manages my affairs, ﴿in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die in submission, and join me with the righteous﴾, meaning from my forefathers.

He lived after that for a week or more, then died at the age of one hundred and twenty years. The people of Egypt competed over his grave, so they placed him in a coffin of marble and buried him in the upper part of the Nile, so that its blessing would spread to both its banks. Glory be to Him whose kingdom has no end.

That is, the aforementioned account of Yusuf (Joseph) is among the reports (anba') of the unseen (al-ghayb), which is what has been hidden from you, O Muhammad. We reveal it to you (nuhihi ilayk), and you were not with them (wa ma kunta ladayhim) — with the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) — when they resolved their affair (idh ajma'u amrahum), that is, they determined upon his plot, (wa hum yamkurun), while they were scheming against him. That is, you were not present with them so that you would know their story and report it; rather, your knowledge of it came to you through revelation (al-wahy).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 12, verse 103:

﴿And most of mankind, even if you should strive eagerly﴾ — i.e., the people of Makkah — ﴿for their belief.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 104:

﴿And you do not ask them for any wage for it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿that you would take﴾; ﴿it is not﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿but a reminder﴾, an admonition.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 105:

﴿And how many a sign﴾ — and how many — ﴿among the signs in the heavens and the earth﴾ indicating the oneness of Allah — ﴿they pass by it﴾ viewing it, ﴿while they turn away from it﴾ not reflecting upon it.

﴿And most of them do not believe in God﴾ — in that they acknowledge that He is the Creator and the Provider — ﴿except that they associate others with Him﴾ — by worshipping idols. For this reason they used to say in their talbiyah (the chant of the pilgrim): "Here I am, O God, You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You, You possess him and he possesses nothing," meaning by it the idols.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 107:

﴿Do they then feel safe that there will not come upon them an overwhelming (ghashiya) punishment from the torment of Allah, or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly (baghta)﴾ — suddenly, unexpectedly — ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ — the time of its coming before it arrives.

﴿Say﴾ to them, ﴿This is my way﴾, and he explained it with his words ﴿I call to﴾ the religion (dīn) of ﴿Allah with insight﴾, meaning with clear proof. ﴿I and whoever follows me﴾ believed in me. It is conjoined to "I" (anā), the mubtada' (the subject of a nominal sentence) about which what precedes it is stated as the predicate. ﴿And glory be to Allah﴾, exalting Him above partners. ﴿And I am not of the polytheists﴾, which is also part of His way.

The Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 12, verse 109:

﴿We did not send before you any but men to whom We revealed⦆ And in another reading, with the *nun* and the *ha'* vowelled with a *kasra* (*nūḥī*, "We reveal"): ﴿to them⦆, not angels, ﴿from among the people of the towns⦆, meaning the cities (*al-amṣār*), because they are more knowledgeable and more forbearing, unlike the people of the desert (*al-bawādī*, the Bedouins), because of their harshness and ignorance. ﴿Have they not travelled through the land and seen how was the end of those before them⦆, meaning the people of Makkah. ﴿That is, the final outcome of their affairs, in their destruction for denying their messengers⦆. ﴿And the abode of the Hereafter⦆, that is, Paradise, ﴿is better for those who are mindful⦆ of God. ﴿Will you not then reason?⦆ With the *yā'* and the *tā'* (as two readings). O people of Makkah, this (is better), ﴿so that you may believe⦆.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 12, verse 110:**

﴿Until﴾ is the endpoint (*ghayah*) of what is implied by ﴿And We did not send before you except men﴾. That is, their help was delayed ﴿until﴾ ﴿the messengers despaired﴾ (*istay'asa*), meaning yaisa, they despaired, ﴿and thought﴾ (*zannū*), meaning the messengers were certain (*ayqana*) ﴿that they had been denied﴾. With the doubled letter (*tashdīd*) on the root, it means denied with no faith after it. With the lightened form (*takhfīf*), it means the peoples thought that the messengers had been made to break the promise of help they had been given. ﴿Our help came to them, so whoever We willed was saved﴾, with the verb pronounced with two nūns, both doubled and undoubled, and with one doubled nūn in the past tense. ﴿Our punishment﴾ (*ba's*) means Our torment, ﴿from the people who were criminals﴾, meaning the polytheists.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 12, verse 111:

﴿Indeed, in their stories﴾ i.e., the messengers, ﴿there is a lesson for those of understanding﴾ i.e., those possessed of intellects. ﴿This Qur'an is not a narration that is fabricated﴾ i.e., invented. ﴿But﴾ it is ﴿a confirmation of what came before it﴾ i.e., of the scriptures before it, ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things﴾ i.e., a clarification of everything ﴿needed in the religion, ﴿and guidance﴾ from misguidance, ﴿and a mercy for a people who believe﴾ — they were singled out for mention because they benefit from it to the exclusion of others.
